artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the positive (negation-free) sentential relevance logic TW₊, whose language is built from propositional variables using the binary connectives → (implication), ∧ (conjunction), and ∨ (disjunction). The axioms and rules of TW₊ are:

Axioms:
 (A1) A → A
 (A2) (A → B) → ((C → A) → (C → B))
 (A3) (A → B) → ((B → C) → (A → C))
 (A4) (A ∧ B) → A,  (A ∧ B) → B
 (A5) ((A → B) ∧ (A → C)) → (A → (B ∧ C))
 (A6) A → (A ∨ B),  B → (A ∨ B)
 (A7) ((A → C) ∧ (B → C)) → ((A ∨ B) → C)
 (A8) (A ∧ (B ∨ C)) → ((A ∧ B) ∨ C)

Rules: modus ponens (from A and A → B infer B) and adjunction (from A and B infer A ∧ B).

Extend TW₊ by adding the following two axiom schemes:
 (Ax L) ((A → B) ∧ (C → D)) → ((A ∨ C) → (B ∨ D))
 (Ax TO) (A → B) ∨ (B → C)

Call the resulting system TW₊ + [Ax L, Ax TO].

The "right-top-or" schema (RTO) is the schema
 (RTO)  (A → B) ∨ (B → A).

Question: Is every instance of (RTO) derivable in TW₊ + [Ax L, Ax TO]?
artifact.status_search_result: According to the source's own theorem, (RTO) is derivable in TW₊+[Ax L, Ax TO] (an affirmative answer is established by showing the stronger schema (IO) is provable there, which yields RTO).

status_evidence.claim: The problem of whether RTO is derivable in TW₊+[Ax L, Ax TO] is answered affirmatively.
